newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak ruling party indifferent to deputy quitting.
newsitem.headline: Slovak ruling party indifferent to deputy quitting.

text.p: Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) said on Thursday it had no regrets over the defection of a senior member of parliament from the ruling party.
HZDS founding member and deputy Frantisek Gaulieder announced at a session of parliament on Tuesday he had decided to quit the party club to protest against the lack of democracy in Slovakia.
"Our club will not suffer from this, but Gaulieder will," Tibor Cabaj, HZDS parliamentary caucus leader, told journalists.
Gaulieder's defection from the HZDS reduced its number of deputies to 60 in the 150-seat parliament.

But the HZDS still has a comfortable majority in parliament along with its two coalition partners, the ultra-right Slovak National Party (SNS) and the ultra-left Workers' Party, which together hold 81 seats.
"There are facts (in Slovakia) which simply have nothing to do with the building of a democratic society," Gaulieder said.

In resigning from the party, Gaulieder, who has a reputation as a dissident and critic within the HZDS, attacked recent privatisations of large companies at prices far below their share prices to groups or individuals of unknown pedigrees.

"We should simply give straight answers to questions of why is transparent privatisation untransparent, why and to whom we sell shares of strategic companies for ludicrous prices," he told parliament.
Gaulieder, a member of the parliamentary committee supervising Slovakia's SIS secret service, said he also quit over lack of clarity in criminal cases with alleged SIS involvement.
This includes the case of Michal Kovac Jr., son of President Michal Kovac, who was kidnapped in August 1995 and dumped outside a police station in Austria.
Two detectives were sacked after their investigations led them to the SIS in the Kovac Jr abduction. A third investigator in May adjourned the case due to lack of evidence.
The case of former policeman Robert Remias, who was killed in a car blast this spring, has also been shelved.
He was the only contact of a former SIS member who said the abduction was organised by SIS chief Ivan Lexa, who supports Meciar in a bitter political feud with the president.
